newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate approves power sector regulator.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate approves power sector regulator.

text.p: Brazil's Senate approved a bill creating a new regulator for the power industry that will oversee the increasingly privatized sector, an official said.

The upper house voted 40-3 in favor of the bill which creates the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL), the official said. The bill now goes to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to be signed into law.
ANEEL will oversee production, transmission and distribution of power in Brazil and its creation is considered a key step in the ongoing privatization of the country's electricity industry.
The agency will be run by a director-general and four directors who will be appointed by the president and whose nominations will have to be ratified by the Senate.

ANEEL will have authority to order utilities to revoke rate hikes it considers unmerited, although the government will maintain power over pricing for an initial three-year period after the agency comes into being.
ANEEL is considered a blueprint for other regulators Brazil will introduce to oversee the oil and telecommunications sectors, which are also being opened up to private capital.
